components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The canonical compact action for saving, submitting, or advancing a task.

components.name: Outline Button

components.description: The shared field vocabulary for source codes, names, selects, and textareas.
components.html: <label class="ds-field-label" for="ds-source">Código de fuente</label><input class="ds-input" id="ds-source" placeholder="gran_encuesta_integrada" />
components.css: .ds-field-label { display:block; margin-bottom:0.5rem; color:#334155; font:500 0.875rem/1 'Inter Variable', sans-serif; } .ds-input { display:flex; width:100%; height:2.5rem; border:1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius:0.5rem; padding:0.5rem 0.75rem; background:#fff; color:#020617; font:400 0.875rem/1.5 'Inter Variable', sans-serif; transition:border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color:#64748b; } .ds-input:hover { border-color:#cbd5e1; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:0 0 0 2px #fff, 0 0 0 4px #020617; } .ds-input:disabled { cursor:not-allowed; opacity:0.5; }

narrative.overview:
The Statistical Desk is an analytical workspace: calm enough for sustained reading, methodical enough for audit, and dense enough to keep definitions, evidence, and actions in view. It behaves like a well-kept working surface rather than a presentation layer; every control supports inspection, validation, or movement through a precise workflow.

The system is sober, precise, and trustworthy. Paper-white content surfaces sit on measured slate layers, Survey Blue identifies purposeful action, and Validation Teal confirms evidence without turning status into decoration. Responsive behavior is structural: the admin grid becomes one column below the large breakpoint, navigation labels hide below the small breakpoint, and type remains fixed rather than fluid.
keyCharacteristics: Work-first density with compact controls, explicit labels, and readable tables.
Quiet tonal layering, fine borders, and minimal ambient shadow.
Restrained accent use reserved for actions, selection, focus, and state.
Consistent radii, spacing, icon scale, and operational language across screens.

rules.name: The Two-Layer Token Rule
rules.body: Brand tokens (`--c-*`) govern authored identity and data-storytelling surfaces; semantic UI tokens (`--background`, `--primary`, `--border`, and their peers) govern reusable controls and shadcn-svelte primitives. On the admin surface, direct Measured Slate utilities are the established local vocabulary. Never substitute one layer merely because two colors look similar; shared components take semantic tokens, while a deliberately branded composition may take brand tokens.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: Validation Teal, amber, and red always accompany explicit status text, a label, or an icon; color alone never communicates workflow state.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter carries every UI role; never introduce a display font into labels, buttons, headings, or data.

rules.name: The Code-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for literal codes, dimensions, schema fields, and source text; explanatory prose remains Inter.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Separate static surfaces with background tone and a one-pixel border before adding shadow; if a card appears to float for decoration, remove the shadow.

rules.name: The Familiarity Rule
rules.body: Use the canonical component variant, height, radius, focus, and icon vocabulary across every task; an equivalent action must never acquire a new visual treatment for flavor.

dos: Do use semantic UI tokens inside reusable primitives and brand tokens only in deliberately authored brand compositions.
Do keep operational detail visible with compact `0.75rem`–`0.875rem` type, `1.25rem` card insets, explicit labels, and accessible tables.
Do state validation, save, replacement, lineage, and publication consequences in text before consequential actions.
Do pair every success, warning, and error color with wording or an icon, preserve strongly visible keyboard focus, and honor reduced-motion preferences when adding motion.
Do keep transitions state-driven and brief: the existing vocabulary is `100ms` for overlays and `150ms` for standard color and control feedback.
donts: Don't resemble a decorative SaaS onboarding wizard.
Don't use oversized generic cards or ornamental progress effects.
Don't hide technical detail or create ambiguous partial saves.
Don't use friendly-sounding copy that obscures validation failures, replacement semantics, lineage, or publication consequences.
Don't add decorative motion that doesn't convey state, orchestrated page-load sequences, heavy inactive-state color, or gratuitous gradients.
Don't use inconsistent component vocabulary across screens, display fonts in UI labels, buttons, or data, or reinvent standard affordances for flavor.
Don't reach for a modal as the first thought; exhaust inline and progressive alternatives first.
